key_insight: Local atomic-swap tests indicate that GNN feature rankings capture physically meaningful neighbor-shell effects, even under deliberate overfitting.
engineering_relevance: Perturbation-based validation can help engineers assess whether materials-model explanations reflect local chemistry rather than compositional artifacts.
method: Train a deliberately overfit, physics-aware GNN ensemble on DFT-derived CoMoFeNiCu decomposition enthalpies.
Constrain output weights to encode feature importance.
Swap individual atomic sites and re-rank features to probe spatial sensitivity.
evidence_signal: Across three stoichiometries and approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways, perturbation effects decayed spatially in a manner consistent with the GNN interaction cutoff.
watch_item: This controlled validation does not establish predictive generalization to unseen compositions or other alloy chemistries.
paper_title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
